def merge3Sorted(p: list[int], q: list[int], c: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    # Merge p and q first
    result = []
    i = 0
    j = 0
    while i < len(p) and j < len(q):
        if p[i] <= q[j]:
            result.append(p[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            result.append(q[j])
            j += 1
    while i < len(p):
        result.append(p[i])
        i += 1
    while j < len(q):
        result.append(q[j])
        j += 1
    
    # Merge result with c
    merged = []
    i = 0
    j = 0
    while i < len(result) and j < len(c):
        if result[i] <= c[j]:
            merged.append(result[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            merged.append(c[j])
            j += 1
    while i < len(result):
        merged.append(result[i])
        i += 1
    while j < len(c):
        merged.append(c[j])
        j += 1
    
    return merged

def main() -> None:
    # Test case 1: Normal case
    test1 = merge3Sorted([1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6], [0, 7, 8])
    print(test1)
    
    # Test case 2: Empty arrays
    test2 = merge3Sorted([], [], [])
    print(test2)
    
    # Test case 3: One empty array
    test3 = merge3Sorted([1, 2, 3], [], [4, 5])
    print(test3)
    
    # Test case 4: All same elements
    test4 = merge3Sorted([5, 5], [5, 5, 5], [5])
    print(test4)
    
    # Test case 5: Negative numbers and zero
    test5 = merge3Sorted([-5, -3, 0], [-2, 1], [-4, -1, 2])
    print(test5)
    
    # Test case 6: Different lengths
    test6 = merge3Sorted([1], [2, 3, 4, 5], [0, 6])
    print(test6)
    
    # Test case 7: Single element arrays
    test7 = merge3Sorted([10], [20], [30])
    print(test7)
    
    # Test case 8: Already sorted concatenation
    test8 = merge3Sorted([1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6])
    print(test8)
    
    # Test case 9: Reverse order inputs
    test9 = merge3Sorted([5, 4, 3], [2, 1], [0, -1])
    print(test9)
    
    # Test case 10: Large range
    test10 = merge3Sorted([100, 200, 300], [150, 250], [50, 350])
    print(test10)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
